title: Learned multi-omics panel is evaluated against pediatric pneumonia severity
summary: A learned eight-feature panel combined five protein and three metabolite measurements to distinguish mild from severe pediatric pneumonia. The source reports an ROC area of 0.82 in a further 50 clinical samples. This is severity-label discrimination, not mortality prediction, a demonstrated early forecast or a treatment effect.
organization: Shenzhen University; Shenzhen Nanshan People's Hospital

source_review.scope: Original selected computational/clinical or physical Methods, model role, specific Results and limitations read; operational biological sections excluded

evidence.ai_role: The Results attribute feature ranking to a random-forest model, while the Methods describe the selected five-protein/three-metabolite panel entering a logistic classifier. AI credit is limited to learned panel nomination/evaluation, not pathways or treatment mechanisms.
evidence.tested: Initial recruitment comprised 57 affected children and 10 healthy controls. The source describes a 70:30 development/test split and a separate 50-sample clinical validation for the severity panel, with reported AUC 0.82.
evidence.unknown: Exact model ordering differs between Results and Methods and is not fully reconciled. Matched multi-omics sample counts, repeated-sample independence and additional cohort timing/composition are incompletely specified in reviewed passages. Some redundancy filtering is described before the split. Validation is retrospective and single-centre, not an established independently frozen clinical test. A heading mentions mortality, but modeled labels are mild versus severe disease. Operational laboratory/pathogen procedures were not inspected.
